texts.preamble: Sudhir Kapoor And Anr vs State Of Uttarakhand And Anr on 31 July, 2017 Author: V.K. Bist Bench: V.K. Bist In The High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital Criminal Writ Petition No.1046 of 2012 Sudhir Kapoor & another ......Petitioners Versus State of Uttarakhand & another ...Respondents Mr. Jagdish Chandra Belwal and Mr. Suresh Kumar Mishra, Advocates for the petitioners. Mr. Pratiroop Pandey, Aga for the State of Uttarakhand.
texts.facts: 2. Present petition has been filed for the following relief: "i. Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of certiorari quashing the impugned order (annexure-4) dated 24.09.2012 passed by respondent no.2 in case no.51/5 of 2012 State of Uttarakhand vs. Chandra Kishore and others." 3. Section 70 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as the Act) provides for establishment of the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal to hear appeals from the decisions of the Adjudicating Officer under section 68 of the Act. At the time when order dated 24.09.2012 was passed, Food Safety Appellate Tribunal was not functioning. Therefore, the petitioner had no efficacious alternative remedy except to approach this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India. The writ petition filed by the petitioner was entertained and on 01.11.2012 following order was passed:- Since the petition filed by the petitioner is pending from the year 2012 and at that Sudhir Kapoor And Anr vs State Of Uttarakhand And Anr on 31 July, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87439967/
texts.arguments: Those Special Courts are constituted u/s 74 of the Act for the purposes of trial of offences Sudhir Kapoor And Anr vs State Of Uttarakhand And Anr on 31 July, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87439967/ 1 relating to grievous injury or death of the consumer for which punishment of imprisonment for more than three years has been prescribed under the Act. The said Section further provides that these special courts shall be constituted by the Central or the State Government, as the case may be, with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court. Learned counsel has argued that the present petition has been filed assailing the adjudication done by the Additional District Magistrate of District U.S. Nagar u/s 68 of the Act and against such adjudication, the appeal shall be preferred before the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal established u/s 70 of the Act. A further enactment has been made that against the judgment of Tribunal, an appeal can be preferred before the High Court, as envisaged u/s 71(6) of the Act. Learned counsel has argued that since no such Tribunal has been established in the State of Uttarakhand within the meaning of Section 70 of the Act, thus, the petitioners have no option but to approach this Court by way of instant petition u/s 226/227 of the Constitution of India, against the order of Adjudicating Officer, who is of the rank of Additional District Magistrate. Today learned counsel for the parties submit that Food Safety Tribunal has already been established at Haldwani. 5. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that he may be permitted to withdraw the writ petition enabling him to approach Food Safety Tribunal.
